text: Doomlings: Venomous now moves only after you play its extra trait, and Lonely Age really limits you to one trait per turn.
Age of Peace now really ignores action cards: no more "stop this action?" prompts for actions that won't happen.
Prosperity: you can now end your turn without stabilizing.
Yes/No prompts (like Age of Exploration's discard-to-draw) now show your hand.
"Each player" ages like Age of Exploration now ask every player, not just the first.
Reaction prompts show the card art, and you can tap (i) to read a reaction card before choosing it.
Phone layout is more compact, so your whole trait pile fits without scrolling.
Swiping between cards in Doomlings no longer freezes the game.
Tap 4 talks to you properly now: "You win!" instead of "You wins!", "You pick up" instead of "You picks up", and so on.
Tap 4: at the end of a round, everyone's leftover cards, including face-down ones, are flipped so you can see what you had.
Tap 4 and Flip 7: it's now obvious you can tap your seat on the start screen and type your own name.
Paydirt: the Home team picker now shows both team names, not "Team 1" for the first one.
Paydirt: the in-game menu buttons are readable now (they were pale text on a pale background).
Paydirt: after each play the dice roll, the result fades in and the ball slides down the field, so you can follow what happened.
Paydirt: calling a play now starts with Run, Pass or Kick, then shows those plays with their average yards.
Paydirt: the field now stays put like a TV broadcast, with each team defending its own end zone, so the ball moves left or right depending on who has it.
Doomlings: on the Final scores screen, tap any player to see exactly which cards and bonuses made up their score, or tap Replay scoring to watch it again. Ties now show every winner.
Paydirt: touchdowns, turnovers and big plays now get their own splashy banner and a flash on the field, so the big moments feel big.
Farkle: the in-game menu is readable now (it was white text on a cream background).
Farkle: the scoring chart now sits right under the buttons, and the combos your roll can make light up so you know which dice to grab.
Yahtzee: the in-game menu is readable now (it was white text on a cream background).
Yahtzee: new layout. The dice sit in one row and spin in place, held dice light up and slide to the left, and the scorecard shows Upper and Lower side by side so it all fits on screen.
Skip-Bo: you can now discard onto a pile that already has cards. Tap a hand card, then tap the pile to stack it there and end your turn.
